newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases as buyers hold out.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases as buyers hold out.

text.p: Investors holding out from the market contributed to prevailing bearish sentiment, and the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index fell marginally on Friday, bourse officials said.
The index lost 8.37 points to close at 3380.42.
Turnover was posted at 23.404 million shillings on 411,226 shares compared to 39.461 million shillings on 2,395,661 shares on Thursday.
"Most of the shares suffered minor losses," a bourse official said.
"Buyers are sitting tight, hoping to get a better price at lower levels," a broker said.
Motor company CMC Holdings and Kenya Commercial Bank traded on the one-hour special board. They traded 54,400 shares at a reserve price of 85 from 83 and 55,900 shares at 97.50 from 95 respectively.

"CMC generates interest every time a big lot is traded because people are watching out for a takeover," a broker said, adding that the struggle for control of the company was between two opposing groups which owned 80 percent of the company between them.
Shares on other boards on average were mixed at low levels.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 112 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 47 unchanged. Kenya Power & Lighting traded at 115 unchanged while Rea Vipingo Plantations eased to 9.60 from 9.65.
Kenya Airways traded at 8.55 from 8.50 while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 36.25 from 36.
British American Tobacco (BAT) Kenya eased to 63 from 64 while Kenya Breweries was unchanged at 58.
